meta.mantra: Technique first. Control second. Weight third.

trainee.name: Lucas
trainee.notes: 14, prefers machines and a clear, predictable plan. Autism-friendly UI required.

coach.name: Dad (Gary)
coach.notes: Views sessions remotely; can set videos/photos and the plan.

meta.effort_model: Reps in reserve (RIR). Normal working sets leave 2-3 reps in the tank; Build Day leaves 3-4.
meta.progression_model: Double progression: add reps to the top of the range at the target RIR with clean technique, THEN add the smallest load increment, then rebuild reps.

technique_colours.red: Stop, reduce weight, or ask for help

safety_rules: Never train through sharp or joint pain - stop the set and tell Dad.
No free-weight bent-forward lifts (barbell deadlift/good morning). If a machine is busy, use the exercise's 'easier option', never a bent-forward barbell lift.
Back extension starts bodyweight; a held plate is only added after clean technique + ~3 RIR, and Dad checks first.
meta.anatomy_data_note: The 'muscles' library and each exercise's 'muscle_involvement' are authored from standard anatomy references (e.g. Gray's Anatomy; standard kinesiology texts) as a starter dataset. Treat as coach-verifiable, not clinical. For richer/verified assets see anatomy_sources.

anatomy_sources.name: Z-Anatomy
anatomy_sources.what: Open 3D anatomy atlas (muscle meshes) derived from BodyParts3D; exportable from Blender to glTF for in-browser 3D.
anatomy_sources.licence: CC-BY-SA 4.0 (attribution + share-alike on any distributed derivative)

anatomy_sources.name: OpenSim / SimTK musculoskeletal models
anatomy_sources.what: Models represent each muscle as origin/insertion + via/wrapping points = real line-of-action (line-of-pull) coordinates; a 'Muscle Force Direction' plugin extracts lines of action.
anatomy_sources.licence: Open-source platform; cite each model's paper (e.g. Delp 1990 lower-extremity).

meta.do_not_copy: Do NOT copy, trace, screen-capture or reuse assets or animations from commercial apps such as Muscle & Motion. Build original 2D SVGs or use the openly-licensed sources above with correct attribution.
meta.muscle_visual_plan: No in-app muscle diagrams for now (accuracy over having a picture). Companion: Muscle & Motion (coach subscription) used alongside the app for visuals. In-app visuals are deferred to the accurate open-3D route (see meta.anatomy_sources). The muscle text data below (origin/insertion/action/line-of-pull + roles) is still used in-app.

vision.title: My why
vision.statement: Build a strong, athletic, healthy physique I'm proud of - and be able to USE it (pull-ups, athleticism, fitness), not just look it.
vision.images_caption: Inspiration physiques & athleticism - the look and capability Lucas is working toward.
vision.images_note: Coach supplies these images themselves, in-app, as private personal-use motivation. Do NOT bundle, scrape or fetch copyrighted photos of real people into the app or seed - the app stores coach-uploaded images only.
vision.framing: Show as a 'north star' / inspiration, not a daily measuring stick. Pair with the process goals (pull-up ladder, strength PRs, consistency) so the focus stays on the work that gets him there.

process_milestones.label: Train consistently
process_milestones.detail: Aim for most of the 5 sessions most weeks. Showing up is the win.

process_milestones.label: Pull-up ladder
process_milestones.detail: Work from assisted pull-ups toward your first bodyweight pull-up, then weighted - ties straight to the athletic look you're after.

process_milestones.label: Get stronger on the big lifts
process_milestones.detail: Add reps then weight (double progression) on the presses, rows, leg press and hip thrust. Celebrate every PR.

process_milestones.label: Look after recovery
process_milestones.detail: Sleep well and fuel your training. Muscle is built while you recover.

goals.coach_note: Trackable goals are process/performance (things Lucas controls); the physique is the inspiration behind them, not a daily measuring stick. Keep it positive - no body-fat, weight or aesthetic-ranking targets.

events.name: Arnold Sports Festival UK
events.goal: Walk in strong, fit and proud of the work you've put in.
events.note: Date is the published Arnold UK 2027 edition (late March, not May). Coach to confirm exact date/tickets at arnoldsportsuk.com; fully editable.

theme.inspiration: Bold, minimal, high-energy athletic look (Gymshark-style energy). ORIGINAL assets only.
theme.ip_guardrail: Do NOT use Gymshark's logo, wordmark, shark icon, trademarked slogans or any brand assets, and do not imply any affiliation or endorsement. Build an original theme merely INSPIRED by that athletic aesthetic.

type.font: Bold modern sans-serif (e.g. Inter or Montserrat)
type.scale: Large, confident sizes; heavy headings; generous spacing
type.note: Body text stays >=18px per accessibility rules.

theme.motion: Minimal and consistent; respect prefers-reduced-motion; no flashing or aggressive transitions
theme.accessibility: The dark theme MUST keep WCAG AA contrast and stay uncluttered - bold but calm. All app-wide autism-friendly rules still apply.

Lengthened.meaning: The muscle is long and under load (worked while stretched).

Mid-range.meaning: The muscle works through its normal middle range.

Shortened.meaning: The muscle finishes fully contracted, with a hard squeeze.

Trunk.meaning: Trains the trunk to stay stable (resist twisting or bending).

Full-range.meaning: A deep stretch at the bottom to a full squeeze at the top.

metrics.label: Bodyweight
metrics.note: Optional. Keep neutral - a data point, not a target.

metrics.label: Calories (optional)
metrics.note: Optional quick number, or sum from the food diary. Descriptive only - no targets or limits.

pectoralis_major.name: Pectoralis major (chest)
pectoralis_major.origin: Medial half of clavicle, sternum, and costal cartilages of ribs 1-6
pectoralis_major.insertion: Lateral lip of the bicipital groove of the humerus (upper arm bone)
pectoralis_major.action: Draws the arm forward and across the body; internally rotates the shoulder
pectoralis_major.line_of_pull: A broad fan from the chest to the front of the upper arm — fibres pull the arm in toward the midline.
pectoralis_major.note: Clavicular (upper) and sternal (lower) heads can be biased by the press angle.

anterior_deltoid.name: Front deltoid
anterior_deltoid.action: Raises the arm to the front; assists pressing
anterior_deltoid.line_of_pull: Front of the shoulder down to the mid upper-arm.

lateral_deltoid.name: Side deltoid
lateral_deltoid.action: Raises the arm out to the side (abduction)
lateral_deltoid.line_of_pull: Straight down the outside of the arm — strongest with the arm already out to the side (shortened).

posterior_deltoid.name: Rear deltoid
posterior_deltoid.action: Draws the arm backward and out (horizontal abduction); external rotation
posterior_deltoid.line_of_pull: Back of the shoulder to the mid upper-arm — pulls the arm rearward.

supraspinatus.name: Supraspinatus (rotator cuff)
supraspinatus.action: Starts the first part of raising the arm; holds the ball in the socket
supraspinatus.line_of_pull: Over the top of the shoulder to the arm.

rotator_cuff.name: Rotator cuff (infraspinatus, teres minor, subscapularis)
rotator_cuff.origin: Front and back surfaces of the scapula
rotator_cuff.insertion: Greater and lesser tubercles of the humerus
rotator_cuff.action: Rotate the shoulder and, above all, hold the ball centred in the socket
rotator_cuff.line_of_pull: Short muscles wrapping the shoulder joint.
rotator_cuff.note: Key stabiliser on every pressing and pulling move.

triceps_brachii.name: Triceps (back of upper arm)
triceps_brachii.origin: Long head: infraglenoid tubercle of scapula; lateral & medial heads: back of the humerus
triceps_brachii.insertion: Olecranon (point of the elbow) of the ulna
triceps_brachii.action: Straightens the elbow; the long head also helps extend the shoulder
triceps_brachii.line_of_pull: Down the back of the upper arm to the point of the elbow.
triceps_brachii.note: Long head crosses the shoulder, so overhead work puts it on a stretch (lengthened).

biceps_brachii.name: Biceps (front of upper arm)
biceps_brachii.origin: Long head: supraglenoid tubercle; short head: coracoid process of the scapula
biceps_brachii.insertion: Radial tuberosity of the radius (and bicipital aponeurosis)
biceps_brachii.action: Bends the elbow and turns the palm up (supination); assists shoulder flexion
biceps_brachii.line_of_pull: Front of the upper arm across the elbow to the forearm.
biceps_brachii.note: Crosses the shoulder, so an arm-behind-body position lengthens it.

brachialis.name: Brachialis
brachialis.insertion: Coronoid process / tuberosity of the ulna
brachialis.action: Pure elbow flexion (works in any grip)
brachialis.line_of_pull: Deep to the biceps, straight across the elbow.

brachioradialis.name: Brachioradialis
brachioradialis.origin: Lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus
brachioradialis.insertion: Styloid process of the radius (wrist end)
brachioradialis.action: Bends the elbow, strongest with a neutral (thumbs-up) grip
brachioradialis.line_of_pull: From the outer elbow down to the wrist.

latissimus_dorsi.name: Latissimus dorsi (lats)
latissimus_dorsi.origin: Spinous processes T7-L5, thoracolumbar fascia, iliac crest, lower ribs
latissimus_dorsi.insertion: Floor of the bicipital groove of the humerus
latissimus_dorsi.action: Pulls the arm down and back; adducts and internally rotates the shoulder
latissimus_dorsi.line_of_pull: A wide fan from the lower back up to the front of the arm — pulls the arm down toward the hip.
latissimus_dorsi.note: Full overhead reach (pulldown) puts it on a long stretch.

teres_major.name: Teres major
teres_major.insertion: Medial lip of the bicipital groove of the humerus
teres_major.action: Extends, adducts and internally rotates the shoulder
teres_major.line_of_pull: Short line from the low scapula to the arm.

trapezius.name: Trapezius (mid & lower)
trapezius.origin: Occiput, nuchal ligament, spinous processes C7-T12
trapezius.insertion: Clavicle, acromion, and spine of the scapula
trapezius.action: Moves and steadies the shoulder blade; mid/lower fibres pull it back and down
trapezius.line_of_pull: Diamond across the upper back onto the shoulder blade.

rhomboids.name: Rhomboids
rhomboids.line_of_pull: From the spine out to the inner edge of the shoulder blade.

serratus_anterior.name: Serratus anterior
serratus_anterior.insertion: Inner (medial) border of the scapula, front surface
serratus_anterior.action: Holds the shoulder blade flat against the ribcage; rotates it upward
serratus_anterior.line_of_pull: Wraps from the ribs around to the shoulder blade.

erector_spinae.name: Erector spinae (lower-back column)
erector_spinae.origin: Sacrum, iliac crest, and lumbar/thoracic spine
erector_spinae.insertion: Ribs and the transverse/spinous processes up the spine
erector_spinae.action: Straightens and holds the spine upright
erector_spinae.line_of_pull: Vertical columns either side of the spine.
erector_spinae.note: Works as a stabiliser (not to be loaded in a bent-forward lift in this plan).

quadratus_lumborum.name: Quadratus lumborum
quadratus_lumborum.action: Bends the trunk sideways; steadies the pelvis
quadratus_lumborum.line_of_pull: Deep side of the lower back.
quadratus_lumborum.note: Key anti-side-bend muscle in side planks and carries.

rectus_abdominis.name: Rectus abdominis (the "six-pack")
rectus_abdominis.insertion: Xiphoid process and costal cartilages of ribs 5-7
rectus_abdominis.action: Bends the trunk forward; braces against the back arching
rectus_abdominis.line_of_pull: Vertical strap down the front of the abdomen.

external_oblique.name: External oblique
external_oblique.action: Rotates and side-bends the trunk; helps brace

internal_oblique.name: Internal oblique
internal_oblique.origin: Iliac crest, inguinal ligament, thoracolumbar fascia
internal_oblique.action: Rotates and side-bends the trunk (opposite diagonal to external oblique)
internal_oblique.line_of_pull: Diagonal, perpendicular to the external oblique.

transverse_abdominis.name: Transverse abdominis
transverse_abdominis.origin: Iliac crest, inguinal ligament, thoracolumbar fascia, lower costal cartilages
transverse_abdominis.action: Compresses the abdomen — the body's own "weight belt"
transverse_abdominis.note: Deep stabiliser trained by anti-rotation and bracing work.

gluteus_maximus.name: Gluteus maximus (main glute)
gluteus_maximus.origin: Back of the ilium, sacrum, coccyx, sacrotuberous ligament
gluteus_maximus.insertion: Iliotibial tract and gluteal tuberosity of the femur
gluteus_maximus.action: Extends the hip (drives it straight); externally rotates
gluteus_maximus.line_of_pull: Diagonally across the back of the hip — strongest near full hip extension (shortened, e.g. hip-thrust top).

gluteus_medius.name: Gluteus medius
gluteus_medius.action: Abducts the hip; steadies the pelvis when standing on one leg
gluteus_medius.note: Stabiliser — keeps the pelvis level in squats, carries, side planks.

biceps_femoris.name: Biceps femoris (outer hamstring)
biceps_femoris.origin: Long head: ischial tuberosity (sit-bone); short head: linea aspera of the femur
biceps_femoris.insertion: Head of the fibula (outer lower leg)
biceps_femoris.action: Bends the knee; the long head extends the hip
biceps_femoris.line_of_pull: From the sit-bone down the back of the thigh to below the knee.
biceps_femoris.note: Two-joint: hip angle changes its length — a flexed hip (seated) lengthens it.

semitendinosus.name: Semitendinosus (inner hamstring)
semitendinosus.insertion: Pes anserinus on the medial (inner) tibia
semitendinosus.action: Bends the knee; extends the hip
semitendinosus.line_of_pull: Back of the thigh to the inner shin.

semimembranosus.name: Semimembranosus (inner hamstring)
semimembranosus.action: Bends the knee; extends the hip
semimembranosus.line_of_pull: Back of the thigh to the inner knee.
semimembranosus.note: With the others, lengthens most when the hip is flexed (seated leg curl).

rectus_femoris.name: Rectus femoris (front quad)
rectus_femoris.origin: Anterior inferior iliac spine (AIIS) of the pelvis
rectus_femoris.insertion: Patella, then tibial tuberosity via the patellar ligament
rectus_femoris.action: Straightens the knee and flexes the hip (two-joint)
rectus_femoris.line_of_pull: Front of the thigh across the knee.
rectus_femoris.note: Crosses the hip, so hip position affects its length.

vastus_lateralis.name: Vastus lateralis (outer quad)
vastus_lateralis.origin: Greater trochanter and lateral linea aspera of the femur
vastus_lateralis.line_of_pull: Outer front of the thigh to the kneecap.

vastus_medialis.name: Vastus medialis (inner quad / VMO)
vastus_medialis.origin: Medial linea aspera and intertrochanteric line of the femur
vastus_medialis.action: Straightens the knee; guides the kneecap near lockout
vastus_medialis.line_of_pull: Inner front of the thigh to the kneecap.

vastus_intermedius.name: Vastus intermedius (deep quad)
vastus_intermedius.origin: Front and side of the femoral shaft
vastus_intermedius.line_of_pull: Deep to rectus femoris, straight to the kneecap.

adductor_magnus.name: Adductor magnus
adductor_magnus.origin: Inferior pubic ramus, ischial ramus, ischial tuberosity
adductor_magnus.insertion: Linea aspera and adductor tubercle of the femur
adductor_magnus.action: Pulls the thigh inward; its back portion also extends the hip
adductor_magnus.line_of_pull: Inner thigh, with a hamstring-like rear portion.
adductor_magnus.note: Assists hip extension in squats and presses.

gastrocnemius.name: Gastrocnemius (upper calf)
gastrocnemius.origin: Medial and lateral condyles of the femur (above the knee)
gastrocnemius.action: Points the foot down (plantarflexion); assists knee bend
gastrocnemius.line_of_pull: Back of the lower leg to the heel.
gastrocnemius.note: Crosses the knee — works most with a straight knee (standing calf raise).

soleus.name: Soleus (deep calf)
soleus.origin: Back of the tibia and fibula (soleal line)
soleus.line_of_pull: Back of the lower leg to the heel.
soleus.note: Works most with a bent knee (seated calf raise).

forearm_flexors.name: Forearm flexors (grip)
forearm_flexors.origin: Common flexor origin on the medial epicondyle of the humerus, and the forearm bones
forearm_flexors.action: Grip; bend the wrist and fingers
forearm_flexors.line_of_pull: Along the inside of the forearm to the hand.
forearm_flexors.note: Trained isometrically by holding and carrying loads.

workouts.name: Build Day
workouts.subtitle: Shoulders · Arms · Chest · Calves · Carries · Easy fitness

leg_press.name: 45-degree Leg Press
leg_press.position_why: This exercise loads the thighs hardest deep in the stretched position.
leg_press.trains: Thighs (quadriceps) and glutes. A safe way to load your legs hard without balancing a bar.
leg_press.find_equipment: A large angled machine with a padded seat low down and a flat footplate up above you. You push the footplate away by straightening your legs.
setup: Set the seat so your knees are bent to roughly 90 degrees when your feet are on the plate.
Load a weight you can control for the bottom of the rep range.
Sit fully back so your whole back and hips are on the pad.
Place both feet flat on the plate, about hip-to-shoulder width apart, mid-height.
Release the safety handles only once your feet are set.
starting_position: Feet: flat on the plate, evenly spread across the whole foot.
Back and hips: pressed into the pad, no gap under your lower back.
Hands: hold the side handles lightly.
Head: resting back, looking forward.
how_to_rep: Push the plate away by straightening your legs. Do not lock your knees hard at the top.
Breathe out as you push.
Lower for about two to three seconds until your knees reach about 90 degrees.
Breathe in as you lower.
Stop lowering before your hips or lower back start to curl up off the pad.
leg_press.feel_do: Effort in the fronts of your thighs and your glutes.
leg_press.feel_dont: You should not feel sharp pain in your knees or lower back.
common_mistakes: Letting the hips roll up off the seat at the bottom (you went too deep).
Bouncing at the bottom to start the next rep.
Knees caving inwards — keep them tracking over your feet.
Snapping the knees straight and locking them hard at the top.
stop_set_when: Your hips begin to lift off the seat at the bottom.
You have completed the planned reps.
The next rep would need a bounce, swing or twist to finish.
The movement gets shorter just to keep going.
Fewer than two clean reps look likely.
You feel sharp pain, joint pain or anything unusual.
leg_press.easier_option: Use a lighter weight and a slightly smaller range (do not go quite as deep).
leg_press.progress_when: When every set reaches the top of the rep range with control and about two reps left, add the smallest weight increase.
leg_press.video_search_query: 45 degree leg press machine how to proper form beginner

chest_press.name: Seated Chest Press Machine
chest_press.position_why: This exercise works the chest through its strong middle range.
chest_press.trains: Chest, front of the shoulders and triceps.
chest_press.find_equipment: A seated machine with a back pad and two handles in front of your chest. You push the handles forward, away from your body.
setup: Set the seat height so the handles line up with the middle of your chest.
Set the seat depth so your back is flat on the pad and your arms are not stretched too far back at the start.
Select the weight.
starting_position: Back: flat against the pad the whole set.
Feet: flat on the floor.
Hands: hold the handles at chest height, wrists straight (not bent back).
Shoulders: pull your shoulder blades gently down and back into the pad before you push.
how_to_rep: Push the handles straight forward until your arms are almost straight. Do not lock the elbows hard.
Breathe out as you push.
Lower for about two to three seconds until your hands are back level with your chest.
Breathe in as you lower.
Keep your shoulder blades down and back — do not let your shoulders roll forward off the pad.
chest_press.feel_do: Effort across your chest, front shoulders and the backs of your arms.
chest_press.feel_dont: You should not feel pinching at the front of the shoulder.
common_mistakes: Letting the shoulders roll forward off the pad as you push.
Bending the wrists back under the load.
Bouncing the handles at the chest.
Only doing half the range — push almost fully out and return fully.
stop_set_when: Your shoulders start to roll forward off the pad to finish a rep.
You have completed the planned reps.
The next rep would need a bounce, swing or twist to finish.
The movement gets shorter just to keep going.
Fewer than two clean reps look likely.
You feel sharp pain, joint pain or anything unusual.
chest_press.easier_option: Reduce the weight, or use a slightly smaller range at the chest end if the stretch feels too much.
chest_press.progress_when: When every set hits the top of the range with control and about two reps left, add the smallest increase.
chest_press.video_search_query: seated chest press machine how to proper form

shoulder_press.name: Seated Shoulder Press Machine
shoulder_press.position_why: This exercise a compound press through the middle range.
shoulder_press.find_equipment: A seated machine with a back pad and handles at about shoulder height. You press the handles up overhead.
setup: Set the seat so the handles start at about shoulder height, not far below or above.
Select the weight.
Sit tall with your back on the pad.
starting_position: Back: against the pad, ribs down (do not arch hard).
Feet: flat on the floor.
Hands: on the handles at shoulder height, wrists straight.
Head: tall, looking forward.
how_to_rep: Press the handles up until your arms are almost straight. Do not lock hard.
Breathe out as you press up.
Lower for about two to three seconds back to shoulder height.
Breathe in as you lower.
Keep your ribs down — do not lean back and turn it into a chest press.
shoulder_press.feel_do: Effort in the shoulders and the backs of the arms.
shoulder_press.feel_dont: You should not feel neck strain or shoulder pinching.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back and leaning back to push the weight up.
Shrugging the shoulders up to the ears.
Only pressing halfway up.
Pushing the head forward.
stop_set_when: You start arching your back to move the weight.
You have completed the planned reps.
The next rep would need a bounce, swing or twist to finish.
The movement gets shorter just to keep going.
Fewer than two clean reps look likely.
You feel sharp pain, joint pain or anything unusual.
shoulder_press.easier_option: Reduce the weight, or use the neutral-grip (palms-facing) handles if available.
shoulder_press.progress_when: When every set reaches the top of the range with control and about two reps left, add the smallest increase.
shoulder_press.video_search_query: seated shoulder press machine how to proper form

shoulder_press_neutral.name: Neutral-Grip Shoulder Press Machine
shoulder_press_neutral.position_why: This exercise a comfortable compound press through the middle range.
shoulder_press_neutral.trains: Shoulders and triceps. The palms-facing grip is often more comfortable for the shoulders.
shoulder_press_neutral.find_equipment: A seated overhead-press machine where the handles let your palms face each other, rather than facing forward.
setup: Set the seat so the handles start at about shoulder height.
Choose the neutral (palms-facing) handles.
Select the weight.
starting_position: Back: against the pad, ribs down.
Feet: flat on the floor.
Hands: palms facing each other, wrists straight.
Head: tall, looking forward.
how_to_rep: Press up until your arms are almost straight. Do not lock hard.
Breathe out as you press up.
Lower for about two to three seconds to shoulder height.
Breathe in as you lower.
Keep your ribs down; do not lean back.
shoulder_press_neutral.feel_do: Effort in the shoulders and the backs of the arms.
shoulder_press_neutral.feel_dont: You should not feel neck strain or shoulder pinching.
common_mistakes: Leaning back and arching to lift the weight.
Shrugging the shoulders to the ears.
Pressing only halfway up.
Letting the wrists bend back.
stop_set_when: You start arching your back to move the weight.
You have completed the planned reps.
The next rep would need a bounce, swing or twist to finish.
The movement gets shorter just to keep going.
Fewer than two clean reps look likely.
You feel sharp pain, joint pain or anything unusual.
shoulder_press_neutral.easier_option: Reduce the weight, or use the standard seated shoulder press.
shoulder_press_neutral.progress_when: When every set hits the top of the range with control and about two reps left, add the smallest increase.
shoulder_press_neutral.video_search_query: neutral grip shoulder press machine proper form

leg_ext.name: Leg Extension Machine
leg_ext.position_why: This exercise hardest at the top, where the thigh is fully contracted.
leg_ext.find_equipment: A seated machine with a back pad and a padded roller on the front of your lower shins. You straighten your knees to lift the roller.
setup: Set the seat so the back of your knee lines up with the machine's pivot point.
Set the shin pad so it rests just above your feet, on the lower shin.
Select the weight.
starting_position: Back: against the pad.
Knees: lined up with the machine pivot.
Feet/shins: behind the roller pad.
Hands: hold the side handles.
how_to_rep: Straighten your knees to lift the pad until your legs are nearly straight.
Breathe out as you lift.
Pause for a moment at the top without snapping the knees.
Lower for about two to three seconds under control.
Breathe in as you lower.
leg_ext.feel_do: Effort in the fronts of the thighs.
leg_ext.feel_dont: You should not feel sharp pain behind or inside the kneecap.
common_mistakes: Swinging the torso back to fling the weight up.
Dropping the weight fast on the way down.
Only lifting halfway.
Lifting the hips off the seat.
stop_set_when: You have to swing your body to lift the pad.
You have completed the planned reps.
The next rep would need a bounce, swing or twist to finish.
The movement gets shorter just to keep going.
Fewer than two clean reps look likely.
You feel sharp pain, joint pain or anything unusual.
leg_ext.easier_option: Reduce the weight and control the lowering phase.
leg_ext.progress_when: When every set reaches the top of the range with control and about two reps left, add the smallest increase.
leg_ext.video_search_query: leg extension machine proper form beginner

lateral_raise.name: Machine Lateral Raise
lateral_raise.position_why: This exercise hardest at the top, where the shoulder is contracted.
lateral_raise.trains: The side of the shoulders, which makes them look wider.
lateral_raise.find_equipment: A machine where pads sit against your outer upper arms and you lift out to the sides against them.
setup: Set the seat so the pads sit on your outer upper arms and the pivot is near your shoulder.
Select a light weight — this is a small muscle.
starting_position: Body: tall and still.
Outer arms: against the pads.
Hands: resting on the handles.
Shoulders: relaxed, not shrugged.
how_to_rep: Lift out to the side until your arms are about level with your shoulders — no higher.
Breathe out as you lift.
Lead with your elbows, not your hands.
Lower for about two to three seconds under control.
Breathe in as you lower.
lateral_raise.feel_do: Effort on the sides of the shoulders.
lateral_raise.feel_dont: You should not feel it mainly in your neck or upper traps.
common_mistakes: Using too much weight and heaving with the body.
Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears.
Lifting far above shoulder height.
Rushing the lowering phase.

Hands: holding the rope ends, palms facing each other.
Body: tall and still.
how_to_rep: Curl the rope up toward your shoulders, keeping your palms facing each other.
Breathe out as you curl up.
Keep your upper arms still — only the forearms move.
Lower for about two to three seconds until your arms are straight.
Breathe in as you lower.
hammer_curl.feel_do: Effort in the biceps and forearms.
hammer_curl.feel_dont: You should not feel it in your lower back.
common_mistakes: Swinging the body.
Letting the elbows drift forward.
Only curling halfway.
Rushing the lowering.
stop_set_when: You have to swing your body to lift the rope.
You have completed the planned reps.
The next rep would need a bounce, swing or twist to finish.
The movement gets shorter just to keep going.
Fewer than two clean reps look likely.
You feel sharp pain, joint pain or anything unusual.
hammer_curl.easier_option: Reduce the weight and keep the elbows still.
hammer_curl.progress_when: When every set reaches the top of the range with control and about two reps left, add the smallest increase.
hammer_curl.video_search_query: cable rope hammer curl proper form

hack_squat.name: Hack Squat or Pendulum Squat Machine
hack_squat.position_why: This exercise loads the thighs hardest deep in the stretched position.
hack_squat.trains: Thighs (quadriceps) and glutes. A supported squat where the machine guides the path so you can focus on your legs through a deep, stretched range.
hack_squat.find_equipment: A machine you stand in with your back on an angled pad and shoulder pads above you. You bend and straighten your legs along a fixed track.
setup: Set the shoulder pads to your height.
Place your feet flat on the platform, about hip-to-shoulder width.
Select a weight you can control.
Release the safety handles only once you are set.
starting_position: Back: flat against the pad.
Feet: flat, evenly spread.
Shoulders: under the pads.
Head: resting back, looking forward.
how_to_rep: Bend your knees and lower for about two to three seconds until your thighs are roughly parallel to the platform.
Breathe in as you lower.
Keep your knees tracking over your feet — do not let them cave in.
Drive back up until your legs are almost straight. Do not lock hard.
Breathe out as you push up.
hack_squat.feel_do: Effort in the thighs and glutes, including a stretch at the bottom.
hack_squat.feel_dont: You should not feel sharp knee or lower-back pain.
common_mistakes: Knees caving inwards.
Lifting the heels off the platform.
Rounding the lower back off the pad at the bottom.
Bouncing out of the bottom.
stop_set_when: Your lower back rounds off the pad at the bottom.
You have completed the planned reps.
The next rep would need a bounce, swing or twist to finish.
The movement gets shorter just to keep going.
Fewer than two clean reps look likely.
You feel sharp pain, joint pain or anything unusual.
hack_squat.easier_option: Use the leg press from Push A, or a lighter single-leg press.
hack_squat.progress_when: When every set reaches the top of the range with control and about two reps left, add the smallest increase.
hack_squat.video_search_query: hack squat machine proper form beginner

incline_press.name: Incline Chest Press Machine
incline_press.position_why: This exercise an upper-chest press through the middle range.
incline_press.trains: Upper chest, front shoulders and triceps.
incline_press.find_equipment: A seated press machine set at an incline, so you push the handles up and forward at an angle.
setup: Set the seat so the handles line up with your upper chest.
Set the seat depth so your back is flat and arms are not stretched too far back.
Select the weight.
starting_position: Back: flat against the pad.
Feet: flat on the floor.
Hands: on the handles at upper-chest height, wrists straight.
Shoulders: pulled gently down and back into the pad.
how_to_rep: Push the handles up and forward until your arms are almost straight. Do not lock hard.
Breathe out as you push.
Lower for about two to three seconds until your hands return to upper-chest height.
Breathe in as you lower.
Keep your shoulder blades down and back on the pad.
incline_press.feel_do: Effort in the upper chest, front shoulders and triceps.
incline_press.feel_dont: You should not feel pinching at the front of the shoulder.
common_mistakes: Shoulders rolling forward off the pad.
Bending the wrists back.
Only pushing halfway.
Bouncing at the bottom.
stop_set_when: Your shoulders roll forward off the pad to finish a rep.
You have completed the planned reps.
The next rep would need a bounce, swing or twist to finish.
The movement gets shorter just to keep going.
Fewer than two clean reps look likely.
You feel sharp pain, joint pain or anything unusual.
incline_press.easier_option: Use a flat machine press. A supported incline dumbbell press is only for later, after coaching in setup.
incline_press.progress_when: When every set reaches the top of the range with control and about two reps left, add the smallest increase.
incline_press.video_search_query: incline chest press machine proper form

cable_fly.name: Cable or Machine Chest Fly
cable_fly.position_why: This exercise opens the chest into a loaded stretch.
cable_fly.trains: The chest, trained through a wide, stretched arc — the lengthened-position partner to your chest presses.
cable_fly.find_equipment: Either a pec-deck machine (forearms or hands on pads, you bring them together) or two cables set at about chest height with a handle in each hand.
setup: Machine: set the seat so your hands/forearms meet the pads at about chest height.
Cables: set both pulleys to about chest height, one handle in each hand, stand in the middle.
Select a light weight — the stretch makes this harder than it looks.
starting_position: Body: tall, chest up.
Arms: open out to the sides at about chest height, a slight bend in the elbows (this is the stretch).
Shoulders: down, not shrugged.
how_to_rep: Bring your hands together in front of your chest in a wide arc, like hugging a tree.
Breathe out as you bring them together.
Keep the slight elbow bend fixed — the movement is at the shoulders, not the elbows.
Open slowly, for about two to three seconds, back to the stretch.
Breathe in as you open. Control the stretch — do not let it pull your arms back fast.
cable_fly.feel_do: A stretch across the chest at the open position, and a squeeze as you bring the hands together.
cable_fly.feel_dont: You should not feel a sharp pull at the front of the shoulder.
common_mistakes: Using too much weight so the stretch yanks the arms back.
Bending and straightening the elbows (turning it into a press).
Shrugging the shoulders.
Cutting the stretch short.
stop_set_when: You can no longer control the arms smoothly through the stretch.
You have completed the planned reps.
The next rep would need a bounce, swing or twist to finish.
The movement gets shorter just to keep going.
Fewer than two clean reps look likely.
You feel sharp pain, joint pain or anything unusual.
cable_fly.easier_option: Reduce the weight, or use the pec-deck machine (more supported than cables).
cable_fly.progress_when: When every set reaches the top of the rep range with a controlled stretch and about three reps left, add the smallest increase. This is a Build Day exercise — keep it light and smooth.
cable_fly.video_search_query: cable chest fly or pec deck proper form

pallof.name: Pallof Press (Anti-Rotation)
pallof.position_why: This exercise trains the trunk to resist twisting.
pallof.trains: The muscles that stop your body twisting — a key part of a stable, strong trunk.
pallof.find_equipment: A cable set at about chest height with a single handle. You stand side-on and press the handle straight out in front of your chest.
setup: Set the pulley at about chest height with a handle.
Select a light weight.
Stand side-on to the machine, a step away, so the cable pulls you toward it.
starting_position: Feet: about shoulder width, knees soft.
Hands: both on the handle, held at the middle of your chest.
Body: tall and square to the front (do not let the cable turn you).
Stomach: gently braced, as if someone is about to poke it.
how_to_rep: Press the handle straight out in front of your chest until your arms are straight.
The cable will try to twist you — do not let it. Stay square.
Hold for a moment with arms straight.
Bring the handle back to your chest under control.
Breathe steadily throughout; do not hold your breath.
pallof.feel_do: Effort around the sides and front of your trunk as you resist the twist.
pallof.feel_dont: You should not feel lower-back strain.
common_mistakes: Letting your body rotate toward the machine.
Using too much weight so you cannot stay square.
Holding your breath.
Leaning away to counterbalance instead of staying tall.
stop_set_when: You can no longer stop your body twisting toward the machine.
You have completed the planned reps.
The next rep would need a bounce, swing or twist to finish.
The movement gets shorter just to keep going.
Fewer than two clean reps look likely.
You feel sharp pain, joint pain or anything unusual.
pallof.easier_option: Stand closer to the machine or use a lighter weight. Do the same number of reps on each side.
pallof.progress_when: When you can do the top of the range on both sides while staying perfectly square, add the smallest increase.
pallof.video_search_query: pallof press anti rotation core proper form

side_plank.name: Side Plank
side_plank.position_why: This exercise trains the trunk to resist bending sideways.
side_plank.trains: The side of your trunk — the muscles that stop you bending sideways. Builds a stable, injury-resistant midsection.
side_plank.find_equipment: No equipment. A clear floor space, ideally with a mat.
setup: Lie on your side on a mat.
Place your bottom forearm flat on the floor, elbow under your shoulder.
Stack your feet, or stagger them for more balance.
starting_position: Forearm: flat, elbow directly under your shoulder.
Feet: stacked or staggered.
Body: in a straight line from head to feet.
Head: in line with your spine, looking forward.
how_to_rep: Lift your hips off the floor until your body is a straight line.
Keep breathing steadily — do not hold your breath.
Hold the position for the set time (start at 20 seconds).
Keep your hips up; do not let them sag toward the floor.
Lower under control, then swap sides.
side_plank.feel_do: Effort down the side of your trunk that is closest to the floor.
side_plank.feel_dont: You should not feel it in your shoulder joint or neck.
common_mistakes: Letting the hips sag toward the floor.
Rolling forward or backward out of a straight line.
Holding your breath.
Propping the elbow too far forward.
stop_set_when: Your hips start to sag and you cannot lift them back up.
You have completed the planned reps.
The next rep would need a bounce, swing or twist to finish.
The movement gets shorter just to keep going.
Fewer than two clean reps look likely.
You feel sharp pain, joint pain or anything unusual.
side_plank.easier_option: Bend your knees and rest them on the floor, holding a straight line from head to knees.
side_plank.progress_when: When you can hold 30 clean seconds on each side, add a few seconds. There is no weight to add.

calf.name: Calf Raise (Standing or Seated Machine)
calf.position_why: This exercise a deep stretch at the bottom to a full squeeze at the top.
calf.trains: The calf muscles at the back of your lower legs — trained through the full range, from a deep stretch to a full squeeze.
calf.find_equipment: A machine with pads on your shoulders (standing) or thighs (seated) and a raised platform for the balls of your feet.
setup: Place the balls of your feet on the platform, heels hanging off.
Set the shoulder or thigh pad snugly.
Select the weight.
starting_position: Feet: balls of the feet on the edge, heels lowered.
Legs: straight (standing) or bent (seated), as the machine requires.
Body: tall and still.
Hands: hold the handles for balance.
how_to_rep: Lower your heels below the platform for a deep stretch, for about two seconds.
Then push up onto the balls of your feet as high as you can.
Breathe out as you rise.
Pause and squeeze for a moment at the top.
Control the whole range — stretch at the bottom, squeeze at the top.
calf.feel_do: A stretch, then effort and a squeeze, in the calves.
calf.feel_dont: You should not feel sharp pain in the knees or Achilles.
common_mistakes: Bouncing quickly instead of controlling each rep.
Only doing a small range.
Rushing the lowering.
Rolling the ankles outward.
stop_set_when: You have to bounce to keep moving the weight.
You have completed the planned reps.
The next rep would need a bounce, swing or twist to finish.
The movement gets shorter just to keep going.
Fewer than two clean reps look likely.
You feel sharp pain, joint pain or anything unusual.
calf.easier_option: Reduce the weight and slow the movement.
calf.progress_when: When every set reaches the top of the range with full control and about two to three reps left, add the smallest increase.

carry.name: Suitcase Carry
carry.position_why: This exercise keeps you tall and level — resisting a sideways lean.
carry.trains: Grip, trunk and whole-body stability. You carry a weight in one hand and walk without leaning.
carry.find_equipment: One dumbbell or kettlebell, and a clear walkway.
setup: Choose one weight you can hold with good posture.
Stand tall and pick it up in one hand with a straight back (bend your knees to lift it).
starting_position: Weight: in one hand by your side.
Body: tall, shoulders level (do not let the weight pull you sideways).
Eyes: forward.
Stomach: gently braced.
how_to_rep: Walk slowly and steadily for the set distance or time, staying tall and level.
Do not lean away from the weight; stay square.
Breathe steadily.
Set the weight down with a straight back, then swap hands and repeat.
carry.feel_do: Effort in your grip and the side of your trunk holding you level.
carry.feel_dont: You should not feel lower-back strain.
common_mistakes: Leaning sideways under the weight.
Rushing and losing posture.
Rounding the back when picking the weight up or down.
Doing more on one side than the other.
stop_set_when: You start leaning sideways and cannot stay level.
You have completed the planned reps.
The next rep would need a bounce, swing or twist to finish.
The movement gets shorter just to keep going.
Fewer than two clean reps look likely.
You feel sharp pain, joint pain or anything unusual.
carry.easier_option: Use a lighter weight or a shorter distance.
carry.progress_when: When you can carry the full distance staying tall and level on both sides, add a small amount of weight.

cardio.name: Easy Cardio
cardio.position_why: This exercise light fitness to help recovery.
cardio.trains: Your heart and lungs. Kept easy so it helps recovery rather than adding fatigue.
cardio.find_equipment: A bike, treadmill, cross-trainer or rower.
setup: Pick any machine you like.
Set an easy pace.
starting_position: Body: relaxed, good posture.
Pace: easy — you should be able to speak in full sentences.
how_to_rep: Keep an easy, steady pace for 8 to 12 minutes.
Breathe comfortably.
This is not a race and not a test — keep it light.
If you cannot speak in sentences, slow down.
cardio.feel_do: Slightly raised breathing and a light sweat.
cardio.feel_dont: You should not feel out of breath or exhausted.
common_mistakes: Going too hard and turning it into a hard session.
Making it longer than planned.
stop_set_when: You cannot speak in sentences (slow down) or you reach the time.
You have completed the planned reps.
The next rep would need a bounce, swing or twist to finish.
The movement gets shorter just to keep going.
Fewer than two clean reps look likely.
You feel sharp pain, joint pain or anything unusual.
cardio.easier_option: Reduce the time or the pace.
cardio.progress_when: No need to progress this. It stays easy on purpose.
